Thank you for the time connecting with your office at the FERC holiday festivities last
month.
I am Emerald AI’s senior advisor on power and utilities strategy and was pleased to
have with me at FERC, Emerald AI’s CEO Dr. Varun Sivaram. As we discussed,
Emerald AI is a pioneering technology company, backed by NVIDIA, whose software
makes AI data centers flexible users of power—capable of receiving dispatch signals
from system operators and adjusting the power use of AI computations in tandem with
utilizing any potential onsite energy resources.
Below are some takeaways from my review of the FERC Co-Location Show Cause to
PJM (“Show Cause Framework and Emerald AI Validations”). The Show Cause order
addresses the immediate mechanics of co-location – the information below provides a
picture into the behind-the-scenes tech stack and strategy that will make this possible in
reality, largely backed by orchestration solutions Emerald AI is building and deploying in
the field today at AI factory GPU clusters which benefit from co-located assets, or, no
co-located generation assets.
Emerald AI’s goal is to ensure that there are live projects operating in the field on US
electric grids within the next two years to prove out a flexible fast track for loads with
software-defined flexibility that can help balance the grid with or without 1:1 co-located
generation. In 2025, Emerald AI conducted four demonstrations in partnership with
EPRI, NVIDIA, utilities, and leading AI companies across the United States and United
Kingdom to prove AI power flexibility across four commercial, production-grade data
centers. In 2026, Emerald AI will announce with NVIDIA and Digital Realty the world’s
first commercial-scale power-flexible “AI Factory”: the 96MW Aurora AI data center in
Manassas, Virginia (Dominion transmission and distribution service territory).
We’d be pleased to continue conversations with your office and with technical SMEs on
our work to practically achieve flexibility solutions. Please do not hesitate to reach out
to us for a briefing at any time.


Best Regards,


Arushi Sharma Frank
Emerald AI Senior Advisor, Power & Utilities Strategy
Arushi.sharmafrank@emeraldai.co | alt: arushisharmafrank@live.com
Ph: 571.572.9037

               PJM Show Cause Framework and Emerald AI Validations
Takeaways

     •     Emerald AI’s validations in the field on live data center computation loads
     (training and inference) provide the physical and operational evidence that PJM’s
     proposed "Contract Demand" tariffs are safe. They prove that a co-located load can
     serve as its own "shock absorber," creating a dispatchable reliability asset that sits
     behind the meter but solves front-of-meter constraints with a combination of
     bankable flexibility solutions that include computation orchestration (shifting,
     slowing, pausing, calibrating while assuring required customer computational
     performance) and co-management of dispatch from generation and batteries.
 Emerald’s validations demonstrate that computation load can be a dynamic, dispatchable
resource that can actively manage dispatch risk, effectively serving as its own "locational
dispatch solution” baked into a larger schema for operating computation (data center)
facilities in the novel ways proposed in the Show Cause order (firm contract demand
transmission service; non-firm contract demand transmission service; interim network
integration transmission service).

       1.   Operationalizing "Firm Contract Demand" (Figure 2):

       Emerald’s technology allows for privatization of delivery risk to computation loads
       greater than what a firm grid power ceiling could provide, as proposed in Figure 2.
       The diagram only contemplates that if there is a 100 MW firm service limit above
       which the grid offers no reliability, the customer must bring 900 MW of reliable
       onsite generation to fill the gap. Emerald’s validations (specifically the Aurora AI
       Factory and Nature Energy peer-reviewed data from the Salt River Project demo
       with Oracle, NVIDIA, and EPRI) finesse this logic. By dynamically flexing compute
       power—the firm cap is a dispatch signal around which the developer of the power
       supply can choose to privatize the reliability risk through software controls rather
       than exclusively through hardware redundancy. From the grid’s perspective, the
       appearance of generation to match the load does not change. From the site
       operator’s perspective, the matching of load to generation is a shaping of
       generation dispatch hours and computation flexibility hours, paired together for a
       hyper efficient solution to meet reliability needs without compromising compute
       service-level agreements.



       2.   Figure 3: Making "Non-Firm" (Figure 3) Bankable_ Validating the "As-Available"
       Use Case

       The Show Cause order positions Non-Firm Contract Demand as a backstop
       solution where the grid has no obligation to serve, potentially implying that standard
       data centers cannot function here without 100% redundant backup. Emerald’s
       platform transforms "as-available" service into a commercially viable operational
       mode: the AI factory can actively reshape its demand profile to match the "0 to 1000
       MW" fluctuation shown in PJM’s Figure 3. An AI load can accept a Non-Firm tariff
       without overbuilding diesel infrastructure, effectively privatizing the curtailment risk
       through compute modulation that aligns with the "as-available" reality of the
       transmission system.
 3.    Anti-Toggling (Guarding against unreserved use): Emerald AI’s technology
platform is primed to provide an all-around virtual protection scheme to manage
around regulatory anxiety that a co-located load will accidentally drift into
"unreserved use" during a generator trip or system disturbance, leaning on system
inertia and causing a blackout. The Salt River Project (SRP) demonstration validated
that Emerald’s platform acts as a virtual "protection scheme" or governor. By
successfully cutting power draw by ~25% for three hours during a peak event while
meeting performance targets, the technology provides the mechanical assurance
that the facility will not drift. It ensures the load physically adheres to the
contracted service level, directly satisfying the FERC requirement for strict
compliance with the new tariff boundaries and mitigating the "free rider" reliability
concern.



4.    Locational Dispatch: The AI Factory as a Nodal Asset Based on the Order on
Show Cause section establishing the new Firm Contract Demand and Non-Firm
Contract Demand services (Paragraphs 204–209), the Commission frames the load
modeling as a static constraint at a specific point of interconnection, rather than as
a dynamic, price-responsive node. This is largely the product of the capacity market
construct in which these tariff changes typically live, where PJM plans transmission
and procures reserve capacity for fixed blocks (sinks) of load at specific PJM
buses. Emerald AI’s platform—particularly via the coming capabilities of the Aurora
demonstration site (Nvidia, Digital Realty – Dominion transmission and distribution
service territory, Manassas, VA)—introduces the missing variable: the ability for
site-specific load to actively respond to LMPs and local congestion. While the Order
discusses "curtailment" for Non-Firm service (Paragraph 209), it frames this strictly
as a reliability action ("curtailed during emergency operations"), not as an economic
response to Locational Marginal Pricing (LMP). The service is currently defined by
reservation priority, not by an economic dispatch curve.



A core objective of the Aurora project will be to lean into the dynamic capabilities of
the load, factor that capability into Dominion’s planning, and support similar
outcomes for PJM review—specifically, allowing for a framework to model the site-
specific load as a resource that resolves congestion or prevents it through
constraint management. The core differentiator between how load is planned and
“called on” for economic dispatch in PJM versus ERCOT is also the heart of the
disagreement regarding the reliability contribution of flexible load between PJM and
the PJM Market Monitor. This topic is explored here and arrives at where Emerald AI
believes the markets must land: future iterations of these tariff designs must
 provide RTOs an option to utilize large electronic loads as dispatchable ISO
resources, placing them on the same footing as nodal dispatchable generators.



5.    Grid-Flexible AI Technology Stack - Emerald AI as the Site Orchestrator in
Virginia:



The Aurora project demonstrates a technology stack where Emerald AI acts as the
central orchestrator—the intelligence layer sitting between the site’s internal puzzle
pieces and the utility operator.

•    The Orchestration Layer: Emerald is not just providing software; it is acting as
the bridge between the Site Controller (managing the facility's physical plant) and
the Energy Manager (optimizing cost and dispatch). In this architecture, Emerald
translates grid signals into compute actions, effectively turning the data center’s
server racks into a dispatchable resource that the utility can "see" and trust.

•    Grid Signal Integration: For Aurora, this means ingesting real-time signals

                                           originating from a combination of PJM
and Dominion event calls (aggregating Dominion’s specific rider notices (often
capped at 120–150 hours/year) with PJM’s broader emergency load management
alerts). The site engineering team across Nvidia and Emerald are co-designing for an
insurance band of curtailment hours:




(While Dominion’s retail customer tariff allows for control events of "four to six
hours", the "1.6 hours" average reflects the active response required to shave the
specific coincident peak, rather than the full window of the alert.) Emerald’s
platform automates the response to these signals, ensuring the facility sheds load
instantly without manual intervention.



•     Going Beyond "Cap Flex": While Dominion’s Cap Flex program is designed for
existing customers to flex around known constraints, the Aurora demo factory is a
greenfield opportunity to go further, i.e., handle static curtailment, and actively
      manage local transmission constraints and congestion signals dynamically. This
     moves Cap Flex, creating the sandbox for precision tools that could expedite a new
     project (rather than only cap/limit an existing one looking for more transmission
     capacity).



     •     Validation via Power Quality Metering: To prove this works, the partners will
     install a Power Quality Meter (PQM) at the point of interconnection (a standard
     requirement for every new connection, including this site). This meter provides the
     "truth data" that validates the site's response to grid events, ensuring that when
     Emerald orchestrates a flex down, the grid sees the exact relief it requested.



     6.    Emerald Validation with National Grid UK: The National Grid live trial in London
     in December 2025 with Emerald’s "Conductor" platform introduces true Locational
     Dispatch. Because the AI factory can modulate its consumption in real-time
     (seconds-based guaranteed curtailment response in furtherance of numerous
     system strength/grid need experiments), it provides a counter-flow effect at its
     specific node. In a co-location scenario (Figure 2 or 3 from FERC diagram above),
     this means the AI factory can dispatch itself down to relieve local transmission
     constraints without sole reliance on generation-switching, effectively serving as a
     Non-Wire Alternative (NWA) solution that PJM’s static planning models fail to
     capture.



     7. The "Interim" Bridge (Figure 4): Accelerating Interconnection
     The Aurora reference design is intended to turn the "waiting room" approach
     described in Figure 4., into the final destination. If an AI factory is certified as
     "Power-Flexible" (capable of relieving grid stress), it may never need to graduate to
     the full "Firm Service" upgrades required in Figure 4 noted above. This challenges
     the baseline assumption that "Interim" is just a temporary state; Emerald’s demo
     projects will validate that for flexible AI loads, "Interim" (Non-Firm) coupled with
     intelligent compute modulation is a permanent, stable, and reliable end-state. This
     vision is shared by Emerald’s data center OEM partners and its core investors,
     including Nvidia.


[End of Takeaways Primer: Emerald AI Validations]
